root_cause.text: The error path in __rds_rdma_map() attempted to unpin pages and free the sg list after put_user() failed, even though ownership of these resources had already been transferred to the transport via get_mr(), leading to a double-free or use-after-free vulnerability.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes the `unpin_user_pages(pages, nr_pages)` and `kfree(sg)` calls inside the `put_user()` failure branch, as stated in the commit message: “Remove the duplicate unpin/free from the put_user() failure branch so that MR teardown is handled only through the existing final cleanup path.” This confirms the error path was erroneously freeing resources already owned by the transport.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove redundant and potentially double-cleanup in rds_rdma_map error path, letting the common out label handle it.
intent_record.what: Removed the conditional block that called unpin_user_pages and kfree on error when need_odp is false, within the failure path of put_user in __rds_rdma_map.
intent_record.how: Previously, when put_user failed and need_odp was false, the function would unpin all pages and free the sg array before jumping to out. Now, it directly jumps to out without performing this cleanup, relying on the out label's existing cleanup logic.

grouping_result.intent: Remove redundant and potentially double-cleanup in rds_rdma_map error path, letting the common out label handle it.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly removes the redundant cleanup in the error path that causes double-free/use-after-free, exactly addressing the vulnerability root cause.

candidates.rationale: This condition triggers cleanup of pages and sg list after ownership transfer, leading to double-free or use-after-free.
Unpins pages after ownership transferred to transport, causing potential double unpin or use-after-free.
Frees sg list after ownership transferred to transport, leading to double-free.

vuln_statements.explanation: This conditional check triggers the redundant cleanup of pages and sg list after ownership has been transferred to the transport via get_mr(), leading to double-free or use-after-free when put_user() fails.
Unpins pages that are already owned by the transport, causing a double unpin (use-after-free) since the transport may still access them.
Frees the sg list that has already been transferred to the transport, leading to a double-free when the transport later frees it.

bic_trace_step.reason: The commit adds an error path in __rds_rdma_map after put_user failure (lines +325 to +333) that unconditionally calls unpin_user_pages(pages, nr_pages) and kfree(sg) when !need_odp. However, if get_mr() succeeded earlier, ownership of these resources has been transferred to the transport, so this cleanup causes a double-free or use-after-free. The code does not check whether ownership was transferred before freeing, hence the vulnerable construct is present and not fixed.

bic_trace_step.commit_msg:
RDS: RDMA support

Some transports may support RDMA features. This handles the
non-transport-specific parts, like pinnin
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit eff5f53bef75c0864a5da06bb688939092b848dc
Author: Andy Grover <andy.grover@oracle.com>
Date:   Tue Feb 24 15:30:29 2009 +0000

    RDS: RDMA support
    
    Some transports may support RDMA features. This handles the
    non-transport-specific parts, like pinning user pages and
    tracking mapped regions.
    
    Signed-off-by: Andy Grover <andy.grover@oracle.com>
    Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>

diff --git a/net/rds/rdma.c b/net/rds/rdma.c
new file mode 100644
bic_trace_step.reason: The function __rds_rdma_map() does not contain the vulnerable construct described in the root cause. In this initial commit, after a put_user() failure, the error path jumps to the 'out' label which only frees the pages array and calls rds_mr_put(mr). It does not attempt to unpin pages or free the sg list, because ownership of those resources has already been transferred to the transport via get_mr(), and rds_mr_put() will eventually invoke the transport's free_mr() to clean them up. Therefore, there is no double-free or use-after-free vulnerability in this version.
